out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. The required sign was not provided at the main handsink in the cooking/food prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months. HUQQA LOUNGE (Inspection Date: 09/02/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Cover Foods in Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped or uncovered food in the following location where the food is subject to contamination: large container of ingredients (flour, sugar) were not covered in the storage room. The storage containers have covers, but they were not on the container.
violations.corrective_action: Foods shall be protected from contamination by being stored in packages, covered containers or wrappings unless being cooled. The PIC had the food employee correct this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: rice was 57º and lentil soup was 56º in the hot holding unit which was not turned on.
violations.corrective_action: The EHS educated the PIC on the requirement that TCS foods must be kept hot or cold. The PIC had the food employee reheat the rice and soup to 165º for hot holding.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Restriction & Storage; Medicines Location
violations.observation: Employees' medicines are not properly located to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. A bottle of employee medicine (ibuprofen) was stored on a shelf over the food prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Employees' medicines shall be properly stored to prevent contamination of food and food contact surfaces. The PIC moved the medication during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed a case of oranges stored on the walk-in floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. The PIC corrected this during the inspection by moving the oranges off the floor.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. The food employees (CFM) was not wearing a hair restraint while preparing foods.
violations.corrective_action: The EHS discussed this with the PIC. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months. Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Clean kabob skewers were found stored in a soiled plastic container (trash can) that was visibly soiled and stored on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the soiled plastic container and clean it (keep it clean), and discontinue storing it on the floor. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months. Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: raw chicken was stored over raw beef in the glass door refrigerator and raw lamb was stored with raw ground beef in the same unit.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The PIC corrected both these issues during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: lentil soup and a few other foods prepared on site were not being date-marked as required.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. The PIC labeled the soup an and other foods during the inspection. CDI.

violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: An ice cooling paddle was stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Assignment of PIC
violations.observation: There was no certified food manager present at the start of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A Person in Charge or certified food manager shall be present at the food establishment during all hours of operation. The CFM arrived near the end of the inspection. Recommend having more food employees certified.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The manager could not provide an employee health policy.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS provided the manager with the necessary forms and the model FCHD policy. The manager had all food employees present read and sign the forms. Ensure any other food employees read and sign the policy as well.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the manager with the model FCHD policy which the manager adopted as the establishment’s policy. HUQQA LOUNGE (Inspection Date: 09/08/2025) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no handsoap at the handsink in the prep room with ovens.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The manager provided hand soap at this hand sink.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: in the walk- in, raw meat (beef kabob skewered) were stored over cooked rice and fresh produce.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Move the raw meat to bottom shelves so it can’t contaminate the cooked rice or produce. The EHS discussed this with the manager. The manager had the food employee move the meat.

violations.title: Food Contact with Equipment & Utensils
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found stored in contact with soiled equipment or utensils: uncovered pans of foods were stacked in the walk-in. The bottom of the pan on top was in the food in the pan below.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized or the food shall be in contact with only single-service items. Discontinue stacking pans in this manner. The manager moved the pans during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surfaces Clean to Sight & Touch
violations.observation: The following equipment/utensils were observed soiled to sight and touch: several pan lids in the clean equipment area were visibly soiled.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to the sight and touch. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. These need to be cleaned and sanitized. The EHS discussed this with the manager. The manager said he would have the soiled equipment properly cleaned and sanitized.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Insect Control Devices, Design
violations.observation: Insect control device does not retain the insects within the device. No pest strip type devices were being used in the food prep and warewashing areas, which is not permitted as they can contaminate food and clean equipment.
violations.corrective_action: If insect control devices electrocute or stun insects, the device shall be designed to catch and hold the insects. The manager discarded the unapproved pest control devices.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Observed clean equipment and utensils stored not inverted and on the floor.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean single-service and single-use articles in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor, unless kept in closed packages on pallets, racks, or skids. Correct as soon as possible for before the next inspection. HUQQA LOUNGE (Inspection Date: 09/08/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Multi-Use Food-Contact Surfaces, Smooth/Easily Cleanable
violations.observation: The food-contact surface of the following equipment contains cracks, chips, or pits and can not be easily cleaned: the cutting board on the main food prep refrigerator in the kitchen was severely scored and stained and is no longer usable for food contact.
violations.corrective_action: Multiuse food-contact surfaces shall be: 1) smooth, 2) free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections, 3) free of sharp integral angles, corners, and crevices, 4) finished to have smooth welds and joints, and 5) accessible for cleaning and inspection. Cleaning and inspection shall be completed by one of the following methods: (a) without being disassembled, (b). by disassembling without the use of tools, or (c) by easy disassembling with the use of handheld tools. Replace or resurface the cutting board. It is not longer cleanable as evidenced by the staining on it.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: shelving was lined with aluminum foil, which is not an easily cleanable or durable surface.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Remove the aluminum foil and keep the shelving clean.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Hard Wood
violations.observation: Pieces of treated wood were being used to stack kabob skewers in the walk-in and the food was touching the bare treated wood, which is not safe or approved for food contact.
violations.corrective_action: Wood and wood wicker may not be used as a food-contact surface unless the wood is hard maple or close-grained and used for cutting boards, cutting blocks, bakers' tables, and utensils such as rolling pins, doughnut dowels, salad bowls, and chopsticks. Wood, especially treated wood is not an approved food contact surface. Please remove the treated wood and replace with something that is safe and easily cleanable. Correct as soon as possible or before the next inspection.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: shelving lined with aluminum foil was visibly soiled where it was not covered in foil.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean all the shelving in the food prep area before the next inspection.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.observation: The hot water faucet on the handsink in the kitchen was not working and not hot water was available.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. The manager reported that a plumber has been called and is waiting on a part to be delivered. Correct as soon as possible or before the next inspection.
